Synopsis:
This dialogue is peak Wulbren. If he's met you in haven (after you saved him), he rolls back on how rude he was as he realises the player would be an amazing asset in the city. If this is your first time meeting him since the escape (if haven is destroyed he waits out on the river until this scene in the epilogue), he realises how good the player would be to have on his side in the city and tells him all about how wronged the ironhand gnomes were.

Cluster Contexts:
- SCE_Wulbren.json: Wulbren is the leader of the Ironhand gnomes who was imprisoned in Moonrise Towers and (with the player's help in the jailbreak) escaped during the collapse of the cult’s power — or, if you didn’t meet him earlier in Haven, he fled by boat and only reappears later in the epilogue. Off‑screen he’d been hiding and organising a fraught breakout (gnomes prying at a weak basalt wall, missing tools, tiefling and gnome prisoners still involved), so the conversation assumes recent escape and fragile plans. In these lines he admits he concealed his identity earlier, is freshly impressed that the player felled Ketheric, and now sees the player as a crucial ally in Baldur’s Gate. He also frames the Ironhands as talented inventors long banished and wronged by the city, which motivates his pitch for support.
- HAV_WrootRequest_Wulbren.json: Wulbren is the proud, condescending leader of the Ironhand gnomes and is mid‑counsel with his fellow gnomes (assuming they survived the Moonrise attack) when the player intrudes. Off‑screen the gnomes are likely imprisoned in Moonrise Towers and already cobbling together a fragile jailbreak—prying at a weak basalt wall, improvising tools, and missing equipment while staying wary of cult patrols. The player has already antagonized Wulbren (an earlier insult like “prick” makes him bristle), so his replies will be smug, dismissive, or passively hostile rather than cooperative. Cult sentries or magical scrying eyes (for example the Warden or a half‑orc executioner) may be nearby and able to cut the conversation short, and the exchange can reveal small details about Ironhand tactics and allies (fanatically loyal gnomes like Nimble, anxious savants like Nickles) as well as the wider prisoner situation that includes captured tieflings.
- MOO_Jailbreak_Wulbren.json: Wulbren Bongle is the charismatic, cunning leader of the Ironhand Gnomes, currently held in Moonrise Towers and offering the main quest: free him and the captured tieflings. He can speak through the bars whether the player is locked up or standing outside, and he keeps a tightly‑worn mask of friendly, arrogant charm while probing your motives and nudging you toward rescue (with a faint, controlled hint of menace). Off‑screen the cellblock is under tight surveillance: a sadistic half‑orc Absolute jailer patrols nearby, can telepathically check for tadpoles, control movement, and will report trouble (up to Disciple Z’rell), and the tower is on high alert after recent Execution/Audience events. Several tieflings (Cal, Lia, Lakrissa, and the absent Rolan) are relevant to any jailbreak plot — some in neighboring cells, others restrained elsewhere — and Wulbren speaks like a leader used to giving orders and exploiting weak points (literal or political) while sizing up whether you’re friend or foe.
- UND_GnomeForeman.json: The gnome leader's main dialogue. He thanks you for saving them, and tells you what brought his people to the Underdark to begin with - an expedition led by their charismatic leader Wulbren, to find a forgotten gnomish explosive of awesome power - runepowder.
- WYR_Ironhand_Welcome.json: Gnome S_WYR_Ironhand_Artificer_002 stands near cave entrance into Ironhand basement lab. It greets player with a dialog. If player follows gnomes after checkpoint, they're included in the dialog.

context: Wulbren Bongle is the proud leader of the Ironhand gnomes who was imprisoned in Moonrise Towers and either escaped there with the player’s help or — if you didn’t meet him earlier in Haven — fled by boat and waited on the river until this epilogue. Off‑screen he’s been hiding and frantically organising a brittle breakout: gnomes prying at weak basalt, missing tools and equipment, and several prisoners (including tieflings) still involved in escape plans. Earlier he concealed his identity and could come off as rude or condescending, but now, learning the player felled Ketheric, he’s genuinely impressed and sees the player as a crucial ally for the Ironhands in Baldur’s Gate. He frames his people as brilliant inventors who were banished and wronged by the city—punished for their forebears’ complicity with Sarevok—which motivates his appeal for support. The scene assumes fragile plans and the possibility of nearby cult surveillance or patrols that could cut the conversation short.
